papers.title: Moments of Magic Squares: Line-Sum Conditions, a Permutation Threshold, and Random Energies
papers.abstract: Every semi-magic square of order $n$ satisfies the axial moment identities $\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}j^m=\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}i^m=M(n)\sum_jj^m$ for all $m\ge1$, where $M(n)=n(n^2+1)/2$. For real matrices the converse requires $1\le m\le n-1$, whereas for arrangements of $\{1,\dots,n^2\}$ fewer moments suffice once $n\ge14$. We define the permutation threshold $k^*(n)$ as the least $k$ such that every arrangement satisfying these identities for $1\le m\le k$ is semi-magic. In terms of the column-sum deviations $\gamma_j$, the degree-$k$ conditions state that $\sum_j\gamma_jt^j$ is divisible by $(t-1)^{k+1}$, linking $k^*(n)$ to the Prouhet--Tarry--Escott problem. While Schur's bound on real zeros gives $k^*(n)\le\sqrt{2(n-1)\log(n^4/4)}$, we prove the converse realisability bound $k^*(n)\ge(\sqrt2-o(1))\sqrt n$ (and $k^*(n)\ge(\sqrt6-o(1))\sqrt n$ when $4\mid n$) by perturbing semi-magic squares with complementary row pairs via horizontal swaps. We also show that $k^*(n)=n-1$ for $3\le n\le13$, $k^*(n)=n-2$ for $14\le n\le17$, and $k^*(n)\le n-3$ for $n\ge18$, and determine $k^*(n)$ for $18\le n\le40$ with computer assistance. Finally, at the $k=1$ level of the hierarchy, we specialise the Mantel--Hubert quadratic assignment variance formula to obtain exact means, variances, and limit laws under a uniform random arrangement for the full line-sum energy $E_{\mathrm{full}}$, for the four-term energy $E_4$ combining the first moments and the two diagonals, and for Loly's moment of inertia, and find that $|L_4|=14,639,440$ arrangements of order $4$ satisfy $E_4=0$.

papers.title: Cyclically covering subspaces and additive perfect codes
papers.abstract: Let $h_q(n)$ be the largest codimension of a subspace of $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ whose cyclic shifts cover the whole space. For $r>0$, we characterize the inequality $h_q(n)\ge r$ in terms of cyclic $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear codes over vector alphabets with covering radius one, no nonzero word of block weight one, and a scalar dual generated by the shifts of one word. For $k,m\ge2$, let $I_q(j)$ count the monic irreducible polynomials of degree $j$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$. If $k$ is prime or $m\ge2\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}I_q(j)+2$, we prove that a cyclic $\mathbb{F}_q$ linear perfect code of length $\frac{q^{km}-1}{q^k-1}$ over $\mathbb{F}_q^k$ exists if and only if $\gcd(m,q-1)=1$. When this condition holds, we also obtain \(h_q\!\left(\frac{q^{km}-1}{q^k-1}\right)=k(m-1).\) Restriction of scalars gives the same criterion for every $m\ge2$ when $q$ is odd, $q+1$ is a power of two, and $k=2p$ with $p$ prime. We also show that $h_q(q^k+1)=k$ exactly when $q$ is even, for every $k\ge1$.

papers.title: Asymptotically good codes from Siegel modular varieties
papers.abstract: We construct asymptotically good codes by evaluating Siegel modular forms at superspecial points on congruence towers of Siegel modular varieties. For every genus $g\ge2$ and every fixed weight $w\ge g+1$, the construction gives such a family in sufficiently large characteristic, over a finite field which is independent of the level of the tower. The towers can be chosen so that this field is $\mathbb{F}_{p^2}$. We give an explicit lower bound for the asymptotic rate. The lower bound for the relative minimum distance follows from the Pieri formula on the space of flags in the Hodge bundle and an intersection argument along its strata. We also prove that, for $p\ge5$ and $0\le w\le p+1$, the kernel of evaluation in every genus consists precisely of the multiples of the ordinary Hasse invariant. For $g=2,3$, the geometry of the supersingular locus gives explicit bounds for the relative minimum distance and recovery sets whose sizes are bounded independently of the level.

papers.title: Bayesian inverse problems and epidemic-threshold uncertainty for a heterogeneous SIS reaction-diffusion model
papers.abstract: We study Bayesian inference of persistence from early observations of a heterogeneous susceptible--infected--susceptible (SIS) reaction--diffusion model with standard incidence. We show that the leading prevalence dynamics depend on the unknown coefficients only through the difference between the transmission and recovery rates and the infected diffusivity. The same pair determines the principal eigenvalue whose sign governs persistence, so early prevalence can inform the threshold even when the individual rates remain uncertain. We prove global weak well-posedness and quantitative parameter stability for the SIS system and use the resulting observation-map estimates to establish Bayesian well-posedness. For an initial infection of size $\varepsilon$, we derive a uniform second-order expansion that describes how the separate rates enter prevalence. Incidence depends explicitly on transmission at leading order. When the noise standard deviation is proportional to $\varepsilon$, we prove $O(\varepsilon)$ convergence in Hellinger distance of the nonlinear posteriors to their low-prevalence limits for both prevalence alone and joint prevalence and incidence data. We bound the principal eigenvalue using the growth rate of the infected $L^2$ norm between two times. This rate gives a lower bound for the full nonlinear system, and the upper bound separates spatial transients from nonlinear saturation. Uniform spectral estimates and bounds on infection size and measurement error give sufficient conditions for persistence and extinction. We also bound the error in posterior persistence probabilities under forward and eigenvalue approximation, accounting for posterior mass near the threshold. Numerical examples illustrate threshold inference and the predicted \(O(\varepsilon)\) convergence of the nonlinear posteriors to their low-prevalence limits in Hellinger distance.

papers.title: An Effective Version of Kronecker's Theorem on the Splitting of Polynomials and the $p$-Curvature Conjecture for Order One Differential Equations
papers.abstract: We develop an effective version of Kronecker's Theorem on the splitting of polynomials, based on asymptotic arguments proposed by the Chudnovsky brothers, coming from Hermite-Pad\'e approximation. In conjunction with Honda's proof of the $p$-curvature conjecture for order one equations with polynomial coefficients we use this to deduce an effective version of the Grothendieck $p$-curvature conjecture for order one equations. More precisely, we bound the number of primes for which the $p$-curvature of a given differential equation has to vanish in terms of the height and the degree of the coefficients, in order to conclude it has a non-zero algebraic solution. Using this approach, we describe an algorithm that decides algebraicity of solutions of differential equation of order one using $p$-curvatures, and report on an implementation in SageMath.

papers.title: A cyclotomic Artin-Tate formula and sphere packing for K3 surfaces
papers.abstract: We give new necessary conditions on the Weil polynomial of a K3 surface over a finite field using techniques from the theory of sphere packing. By comparing the Artin-Tate formula over a finite extension, we derive a special values formula at roots of unity that involves the discriminant of the Frobenius coinvariant lattice. Known bounds on the minimum discriminants of even rootless lattices then imply nontrivial lower bounds on these special values. Applying these new conditions to Kedlaya and Sutherland's list of candidate Weil polynomials of K3 surfaces over the field with 2 elements rules out over 50% of the candidates.

papers.title: Non-abelian $p$-adic Hodge theory and stacks
papers.abstract: In the first half of these notes, we survey some aspects of the stack-theoretic perspective on $p$-adic Hodge theory, with an emphasis on the non-abelian aspects. In the second half, we report ongoing joint work on ``quantizing'' non-abelian $p$-adic Hodge theory.

papers.title: Ramification of torsion packets on curves with good-reduction Jacobians
papers.abstract: Let $p\ge5$ be a prime number, $k$ an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$. Write $R=W(k)$ for the ring of Witt vectors over $k$, and $K$ for the field of fractions of $R$. Let $X$ be a smooth, proper, geometrically connected curve over $K$ of genus greater than one. Write $J$ for the Jacobian variety of $X$. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{K}$ of $K$. In the present paper, we prove that if $J$ has good reduction over $R$, then every point $x\in X(\overline{K})$ such that $[\sigma x-x]$ is torsion for each $\sigma\in \operatorname{Gal}(\overline{K}/K)$ is $K$-rational.

papers.title: The $\mathbb Q$-gonality of $X_1(42)$ is $12$
papers.abstract: We prove that the $\mathbb F_5$-gonality and the $\mathbb Q$-gonality of the modular curve $X_1(42)$ are both $12$, improving the previous lower bound of $10$. Since $J_1(42)(\mathbb Q)$ is finite, it follows that $12$ is the least degree in which $X_1(42)$ has infinitely many points. The lower bound comes from an exhaustive search over Riemann--Roch spaces, following Derickx and van Hoeij, using a new reduction by the orbits of a cyclic group of automorphisms of order $12$ on places of degree at most $5$ ($743\,231$ Riemann--Roch spaces). An earlier search with the reductions from van Hoeij's code (about $3$ million Riemann--Roch spaces, about $6$ times more CPU time) gives the same result and serves as supporting evidence. We prove the reductions and record the data needed to reproduce the computations.

papers.title: Periods and CM motives of abelian type
papers.abstract: We associate algebraic Hecke characters to certain invertible motives for absolute Hodge cycles with coefficients in a number field $K$, reversing a viewpoint of Schappacher. These motives $N$ include abelian motives and a new notion of algebraic motive. This Hecke character determines the complex and the $p$-adic periods of $N$, and is determined by the latter; this gives a proof of the Mumford-Tate conjecture for $N$. When $K$ and $N$ are abelian, we prove a refinement of the Gross-Deligne conjecture, as well as $l$-adic and $p$-adic variants. We also formulate a version of the algebraic relations between rational values of the gamma function given by Koblitz and Ogus in terms of a distribution with values in the Picard group of the category of (abelian) Chow motives.

papers.title: A Complete Classification of Maximal Hyperelliptic Curves Related to Chebyshev Polynomials
papers.abstract: Let $\varphi_d$ be the Chebyshev polynomial with $\varphi_d(t+t^{-1})=t^d+t^{-d}$, and let $H_d$ be the hyperelliptic curve $y^2=\varphi_d(x)$. We determine all pairs $(d,p)$, with $p\nmid2d$ prime, for which $H_d$ is maximal over some finite field of characteristic $p$, together with all such fields. For $p\equiv1\pmod4$ only partial results were known. In this case, for odd $d$ we show that the Jacobian of $H_d$ is supersingular if and only if $H_d$ is maximal over a finite extension of $\mathbb{F}_p$, and that this happens precisely when $d=\ell^n$ with $\ell\equiv1\pmod4$ prime and $p$ a generator of $(\mathbb{Z}/\ell^n\mathbb{Z})^\times$; we also compute the Frobenius polynomial. Necessity comes from the Shimura--Taniyama formula together with the non-vanishing of the value at $0$ of certain Dirichlet L-series and information about the action of Frobenius on $2$-torsion. The case of even $d$ and $p\equiv1\pmod 4$ follows from the odd case, by a short reduction.

papers.title: $2$-adic integral models of some Shimura varieties with parahoric level structure
papers.abstract: We construct integral models over $p=2$ for some Shimura varieties of abelian type with parahoric level structure, extending the previous work of Kim-Madapusi, Kisin, Pappas, and Zhou. These integral models are canonical in the sense of Pappas-Rapoport.

papers.title: Pellarin's Identity, Carlitz Period, and Anderson Generating Functions over Arbitrary Curves
papers.abstract: We establish three results for a rank-one Drinfeld module over the coefficient ring of a smooth, projective, geometrically connected curve over $ \mathbb F_q$, with a closed point at infinity of arbitrary degree. First, a Tate-algebra unit exists in the module of special functions precisely when this module is free of rank one, that is, when the period lattice is isomorphic to the module of regular differentials; this proves the Gazda--Maurischat conjecture. Second, under the unit-anchor normalization for an isogeny to a principal-period target, a strictly normalized shtuka product and one characteristic residue give the fundamental period; the same defect equation gives the logarithm residue formula. Third, finite \'{e}tale torsion traces over the field of definition identify the first Frobenius twist of the normalized shtuka differential and express Pellarin's $ \mathcal L(1)$-series at a fundamental period. The source period lattice need not be free.

papers.title: Local Tate duality for syntomic cohomology in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be a local field of characteristic $p>0$. We show that syntomic cohomology over $k$, with coefficients, and defined using Dodd's theory of $F$-gauges, satisfies local Tate duality. We also prove that syntomic cohomology over the ring of integers of $k$, again with coefficients, is Lagrangian with respect to the duality pairing. Finally, we show that, for $p>2$, these results recover Shatz's duality and Milne's orthogonality results for the cohomology of finite flat group schemes of $p$-power order over $k$.

papers.title: Nonnegative weak tilings and the Coven-Meyerowitz condition (T2)
papers.abstract: We develop a general method, in finite cyclic groups, for constructing nonnegative rational functions $f$, normalized by $f(0)=1$, that satisfy the Coven-Meyerowitz condition $(T1)$ but fail $(T2)$, such that $f$ is a weak complement for a set tile $A$. Motivated by the unsupported-divisor questions in arXiv:2507.11672, we show that if a set tile $A$ admits an unsupported divisor, then a suitable dilation of $A$ admits such a rational weak complement $f$. Using this method, we construct an explicit example in the group $\mathbb{Z}_{180}$. The weak complements in our explicit perturbative constructions are not positive definite because of restrictions on the Fourier support of the perturbations. Thus these constructions do not resolve the proposed extension of the Coven-Meyerowitz conditions to positive-definite weak tilings (arXiv:2411.03854, Problem 1.2).

papers.title: Davenport Constants of High-Dimensional Integer Sets
papers.abstract: The Davenport constant of a finite set of integer vectors is the maximum length of an irreducible zero-sum sequence over that set. For nonempty sets closed under negation, it equals the largest $\ell_1$-norm of a Graver basis element of the matrix formed by those vectors. We study extremal and average-case versions in growing dimension, with applications to integer programming. For integer cubes $[-R,R]^d \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$ and the sign cube $\{-1,1\}^d$, totally unimodular encodings improve on the upper bounds from direct circuit decomposition, while random perturbations of Hadamard matrices give new lower bounds. A key ingredient is a uniform affine Bernoulli variant of Nguyen and Wood's surjectivity theorem. In every sufficiently large dimension the sign-cube lower bound is $d^{d/2}2^{-d-o(d)}$, and the integer-cube lower bound is $R^d d^{d/2}2^{-o(d)}$ uniformly for polynomially bounded integer radii. For random sign-cube sequences of even length conditioned on summing to zero, we prove a sharp threshold from irreducibility to reducibility at $d\log d/\log 4$, far below the extremal scale. For fixed $p$ and $R$, we determine exact exponential rates for lattice $\ell_p$-balls when $p=1$, $R\geq3$, or $2\leq p<\infty$, $\lfloor R^p\rfloor\geq3$. For each fixed integer $k\geq3$, we determine the exponential rate of the worst-case $\ell_1$-distance from an optimal LP vertex to the nearest integer optimum in standard-form programs with ternary matrices having at most $k$ nonzero entries per column.

papers.title: The zero-sum constant $\mathsf{s}_p^*$ and inverse problem
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime. We denote by $\mathsf{s}_{p}^{*}$ the smallest integer $l$ such that, out of any given $l$ integers coprime with $p$, one can select $p$ integers satisfying that the sum of the $p$ integers is a multiple of $p$, but not a multiple of $p^{2}$. It was conjectured that $\mathsf{s}_p^*=2p+1$. In this paper we prove this conjecture and solve the corresponding inverse problem. More precisely, we characterize all sequences of $2p$ integers coprime to $p$ in which every $p$-term subsequence with sum a multiple of $p$ also has sum a multiple of $p^2$.

papers.title: Intermediate Growth and Rigidity in Primitive Circulant Spectral Algebras
papers.abstract: At prime graph orders, the complete nontrivial and primitive Fourier spectra of a circulant coincide. We show that this agreement conceals a strong algebraic separation when the graph order varies. For any nonempty finite jump set $S$, let $A_S^{\mathrm{prim}}$ be the algebra of arithmetic functions obtained by evaluating symmetric power sums on the primitive spectrum, filtered by power-sum weight. Removing the common Euler-totient term gives a reduced, locally finite algebra $B_S$, and we prove a filtration-preserving isomorphism $A_S^{\mathrm{prim}}\cong B_S[T_2]$. Thus $A_S^{\mathrm{prim}}$ is non-Noetherian and has Krull dimension one. Its filtered dimensions satisfy $\exp(c_S\sqrt{D/\log D})\leq \rho_S^{\mathrm{prim}}(D) \leq\exp(C_S\sqrt D)$ for large $D$, and its associated-graded Hilbert series is nonrational. Despite agreement on every prime order, the primitive and full spectral evaluation algebras intersect only in $\mathbb{Q}$. More strongly, no nonconstant primitive spectral function is eventually quasirational on residue classes. We give an exact finite-matrix rank formula and determine the quotient obtained by restricting to integers with large prime factors.

papers.title: Reconstructing Numerical Semigroups from Circulant Spectral Dimensions
papers.abstract: The polynomial algebra generated by the spectral moments of a family of circulant graphs consists of all eventually polynomial sequences in the graph order; as an unfiltered algebra, it therefore carries little information about the jumps. We show that its natural power-sum weight filtration retains substantially finer arithmetic data. For a finite jump set $S$ with $\gcd(S)=1$ and $M=\max S$, the relevant invariant is the numerical semigroup $\Sigma_S=\langle M,M-s,M+s:s\in S\rangle$, which arises from the lengths of closed walks winding around the cycle. We prove that the eventual global filtered dimension is $MD+\lfloor D/2\rfloor+1-M(M+1)-g(\Sigma_S)$. Restricting graph orders to $n\equiv a\pmod q$, for $q\mid M$, replaces the genus term by the number of gaps of $\Sigma_S$ in the class $-a\pmod q$; the class $a=0$ gives the genus of the quotient semigroup $\Sigma_S/q$. These formulas yield an inverse reconstruction theorem: the unrestricted dimensions determine $M$, and the dimensions in all classes modulo $M$ at one common stable degree determine the Ap\'ery set and hence $\Sigma_S$. We give effective thresholds, exact examples, and a finite-rank algorithm valid in every degree. Reconstruction of the semigroup need not identify the original jump set.

papers.title: The closure of the nonreal roots of bounded-height polynomials is connected exactly at pronic heights
papers.abstract: Let C_h be the closure of the nonreal roots of integer polynomials with coefficients of modulus at most h. With the nonzero real roots included, the closure is connected at every height; without them, connectedness becomes arithmetic. We prove that C_h is connected exactly when h=q(q-1) is a pronic number 2, 6, 12, 20, ..., and has at least five components otherwise. At height two this confirms a twenty-year-old numerical observation of Shmerkin and Solomyak on double zeros of power series: apart from 1/2 they form the interval $[1/\rho,1)=C_2\cap(0,1)$, with $\rho$ the tribonacci constant. Disconnection is almost always infinite. For (p-1)^2<h<=p^2-3, $h\neq p(p-1)$, infinitely many components with nonempty interior accumulate at $\pm p$ and $\pm 1/p$, and when h<p(p-1) these four points are themselves components. Next to each square q^2>=16, at least two of the three heights q^2-2, q^2-1, q^2 have infinitely many components accumulating at a common point of (1/(q+1),1/q). Explicit series give infinitely many components at every nonpronic height below 167 other than 1, 3, 4, 9, 25, 63 and 81, and in general at most sqrt(X)+1 nonpronic heights h<=X can have finitely many components, although C_h is a Peano compactum at every height. The proofs compare values and derivatives of all admissible power series near a real double zero; the comparison sets are open and closed in the whole core, so components separated near the axis cannot reconnect elsewhere. On the real axis, the double zeros at heights 1, 3, 4, 7 form sets with infinitely many components; at height one this proves a conjecture of Shmerkin and Solomyak and one of Solomyak on the connectedness locus for pairs of affine maps.

papers.title: An elliptic deformation of continued fractions
papers.abstract: We construct an elliptic deformation $\mathcal{Q}_{a,b;q,p}(x)$ of positive rational numbers $x$ by attaching Schlosser's small elliptic weights $w_{a,b;q,p}(s,t)$ to prefixes of Stern--Brocot words. On positive integers $n$ it gives Schlosser's elliptic numbers $[n]_{a,b;q,p}$. Parameter shifts realize $x \mapsto x+1$ and $x \mapsto x/(x+1)$, while a reciprocal parameter transformation gives an inversion formula. The Gaussian degeneration recovers the $q$-deformed rationals of Morier-Genoud and Ovsienko. The regular and negative elliptic continued fractions agree, since they evaluate the same word with the same ordered weights. The numerator and denominator satisfy weighted Farey recursions and, for rationals greater than $1$, are the closure polynomials, or quiver $F$-polynomials, of the associated oriented type-$A$ quivers. Finally, we express the vertex weights as normalized elliptic Euler expressions of balanced virtual torus representations.

papers.title: A Moment Proof of the Hollman-Xiang Conjectures on Kloosterman Polynomials
papers.abstract: Let $F=\F_{2^n}$ and let \[ \mathcal T_1=\{t\in F:\Tr_{F/\F_2}(t)=1\}. \] For an integer $u=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}u_i2^i$ of even binary weight, put \[ L_u(X)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}u_iX^{2^i}, \qquad L_{1,u}(t)=t+L_u(t^{-1}). \] Hollmann and Xiang conjectured that $L_{1,u}$ permutes $\mathcal T_1$ if and only if $u\in\{0,3,6,10\}$. We prove the necessity by a moment method; the sufficiency is their Theorem~4.1. The quadratic moment yields a cyclic autocorrelation identity, while the cubic moment gives a two-variable group-algebra identity. An elimination argument reduces the coefficient word to a monomial or a complementary monomial, and explicit cubic and quartic moments complete the classification. We also prove Hollmann and Xiang's Conjecture~4.5. Namely, if $n>3$ and \[ L_{c,d}(x)=L_c(x)+L_d(x^{-1}) \] is a Kloosterman polynomial on $\F_{2^n}$, then its positive linearized part $L_c$ is injective on both trace fibers. This second result follows from relative quadratic and cubic moment identities and a spectral-zero rigidity argument. Consequently every Kloosterman polynomial is obtained by composing one of $L_{1,0},L_{1,3},L_{1,6},L_{1,10}$ with a linearized map that is injective on both trace fibers.

papers.title: Effective Joint Equidistribution of Subspaces of Bounded Height in Rigid Adelic Spaces
papers.abstract: We prove effective joint equidistribution for subspaces of fixed dimension in a fixed rigid adelic space over a number field. The joint distribution records the rescaled height, the archimedean position, and the shapes of the subspace and its quotient. More generally, we obtain counting estimates for regions in which the height bound may depend on the position and both shapes. Under a H\"older-type bound for the measure of boundary layers, the estimates have explicit power-saving error terms. We apply these results to counting problems involving slopes, freeness, and semistability, and to Diophantine approximation with prescribed shapes.

papers.title: The uncertainty operator, the Weil ground state and the zeros of zeta: a numerical study and conditional positivity of the Weil quadratic form
papers.abstract: Applying the Dirichlet principle to the Weil quadratic form $QW_\lambda$ on $L^2([\lambda^{-1},\lambda],d^*u)$--using only the primes $p\le\lambda^2$ of the Euler product--yields canonical finite-dimensional Hermitian matrices whose ground state has a Mellin transform with zeros proved real in full generality when the lowest eigenvalue is simple and even. While $\lambda^2=13$ gave $50$ zeros of $\zeta$, $\lambda^2=250$ ($\lambda\sim16$) gives the first $1000$ zeros with $>500$ correct decimals (the first with $1341$). We explain this via a correspondence between $QW_\lambda$ and Slepian's time-frequency uncertainty operator $U_\lambda=2-P_\lambda-\widehat P_\lambda$, diagonalized by prolate wave functions with eigenvalues $\delta_n(\lambda)\sim c_n\lambda^{2n+1}e^{-4\pi\lambda^2}$ (Fuchs). Via $\mathcal{E}(f)(u)=u^{1/2}\sum_{n\ge1}f(nu)$ and Gevrey smoothing, $\epsilon_\lambda\le C\delta_4(\lambda)(\log\lambda)^3$ is a theorem (Connes-Kastoris). Computations up to $\lambda^2=300$ ($\epsilon_\lambda(1)\sim10^{-1618}$) show a striking logarithmic coincidence with the Fuchs ladder, confirming this simplicity and evenness. Prolate vectors reproduce all minuscule eigenvectors, and conditioning by them and the pole term removes the minuscule spectrum: $QW_\lambda$ is a direct sum of a finite-dimensional near-radical part (Fuchs ladder) and an infinite-dimensional positive part from the Sonin space ($U_\lambda=2$). Under this ladder hypothesis and $QW_\lambda\ge0$, we bound the ground-state distance to the target with Mellin transform $\frac14\xi(s+\frac12)$ (Hurwitz' theorem). Finally, the semilocal trace formula gives the uncertainty principle via Coburn's lemma and proves, under a hypothesis valid at $\infty$, that $QW_\lambda\ge c>0$ outside a finite-dimensional near-self-dual space, reducing Weil positivity to a Schur complement at the ladder's edge.

papers.title: Bounding the security of the Bromberg-Shpilrain-Vdovina hash function
papers.abstract: The Bromberg-Shpilrain-Vdovina hash functions are a family of Cayley hash functions indexed by an integer parameter $k\ge 2$. Hashes are matrices in $SL_2(p)$ where $p$ is a large prime. We present an attack which finds collisions of length $O(\log p)$ whose average-case time complexity is $O(p^{0.28})$ when $k=2$ and $O(p^{0.36})$ when $k=3$ under an assumption in the spirit of Zaremba's Conjecture on continued fractions. This is an improvement on the more general attacks of Mullan-Tsaban and Slaughter which have average-case time complexity $O(\sqrt{p})$. For any $k$, the average-case time complexity of our attack is $O(p^{1-\delta_k+o(1)})$ where $\delta_k$ is the Hausdorff dimension of a certain Cantor set. This tends to $O(\sqrt{p})$ as $k\to\infty$, so our attack has time complexity comparable to Mullan-Tsaban and Slaughter's attacks as $k$ grows. We give examples of collisions for large primes found by our attack when $k=2, 3$.

papers.title: A counterexample to the Erd\H{o}s--Mahler conjecture
papers.abstract: We disprove a 1939 conjecture of Erd\H{o}s and Mahler by constructing, for every real $\tau\ge4$, a Cantor set of numbers of irrationality exponent $\tau$, each having infinitely many regular continued-fraction convergents of the form $2^a/3^b$.

papers.title: A Threshold-Crossing Condition for the Least Colossally Abundant Counterexample to Robin's Inequality
papers.abstract: We study the constraints that a hypothetical least Colossally Abundant (CA) counterexample to Robin's Inequality would place on the non-trivial zeros of $\zeta(s)$. In the single-prime case we express the least CA counterexample $N$ as $M\cdot p$, where $M$ is its CA predecessor and $p$ is prime. Using the von Mangoldt explicit formula for $\psi(x)$, we express $\ln p$ in terms of a sum over the non-trivial zeros of $\zeta(s)$ and split that expression into its baseline contribution $\mathcal{R}_0(p)$ and its off-line distortion. When both converge, we show that the off-line distortion is negative whenever $1+1/(e^{\mathcal{R}_0(p)}+e^{2\mathcal{R}_0(p)}+\cdots+e^{(v+1)\mathcal{R}_0(p)})\le\ln(\ln M+\mathcal{R}_0(p))/\ln\ln M$, where $v$ is the $p$-adic valuation of $M$. In the case where the least CA counterexample is the product of its CA predecessor and two primes (the semiprime case), the logarithm of the product of the two primes is the sum of two von Mangoldt expansions. An analogous inequality implies that at least one of the off-line distortions of the two expansions is negative.

papers.title: On the equidistribution of eigenfunctions of higher dimensional cat maps modulo prime powers
papers.abstract: The so-called $\mathit{Cat\ Map}$, which is a linear map generated by symplectic matrices $A \in \operatorname{Sp}(2d,\mathbb Z)$ modulo an integer $N\ge 1$ is a classical discrete model of quantum ergodicity. For $d=1$ it has been investigated by P. Kurlberg and Z. Rudnick (2001), J. Bourgain (2007) and A. Ostafe, I. E. Shparlinski and J. F. Voloch (2023). The significantly more difficult case of $d>1$ has been studied by P. Kurlberg, A. Ostafe, Z. Rudnick and I. E. Shparlinski (2025). All these works apply only to almost all $N$ and are unable to provide an explicit sequence of such ``good'' values of $N$. The authors (2026) have given such a construction with a polynomial decay on the corresponding matrix coefficients. Here we use some new ideas and improve this bound.

papers.title: Diophantine approximation with prime denominators in short intervals
papers.abstract: For any real number $x$, let $\|x\|$ denote the distance from $x$ to the nearest integer, and let $\alpha$ be any irrational number. We prove that, for $Y=X^\gamma$ with $7/12<\gamma\le 1$ and $0<\theta<\min \{(12\gamma-7)/24, 1/9\}$, there exist infinitely many $X$ for which there are primes $p$ satisfying $$ \|\alpha p\|<p^{-\theta},\quad X-Y<p<X. $$ Moreover, we obtain an asymptotic formula for the number of such primes. Our result extends the admissible range of short intervals in the corresponding result of Baier and Roy from $2/3<\gamma\le 1$ to $7/12<\gamma\le 1$, reaching Huxley's classical range for primes in short intervals and also improves the exponent $\theta$ in $2/3\le \gamma\le 3/4.$

papers.title: When do all iterates of $x^2 + a$ have maximal Galois group?
papers.abstract: We provide an (in our opinion) simpler proof of the main results of [Stoll1992,Li2020,Li2021] on the question for which integers $a$ the Galois groups of all iterates of $x^2 + a$ are maximal (equivalently, the associated arboreal Galois representation is surjective). At the same time, we extend the results to rational parameters $a$. The main result states that for a subset of rational numbers of relative density $1/2$ in the complement of a certain open interval, the maximality of the Galois group of the second iterate is sufficient for the arboreal Galois representation to be surjective. We also discuss experimental evidence suggesting that a similar statement involving the fourth iterate may hold in general. The results were obtained in collaboration with Claude (Anthropic's AI model); they are also formalized in Lean (except for the experimental evidence).
